fields.description: Distinct from Frappe's own `owner` — an Administrator can raise a requisition on behalf of a department, in which case owner is the Administrator but raised_by is deliberately still set to whoever is actually raising it for that department.
fields.label: Raised By

fields.description: Derived server-side from Equipment Maintenance Settings' capital_purchase_threshold at creation time — informational/reporting only, every requisition goes through the same fixed chain regardless of value.
fields.label: Is Capital Requisition

fields.description: The asset this purchase would replace, if any.
fields.label: Linked Asset

fields.description: The breakdown/repair ticket that prompted this purchase, if any.
fields.label: Linked Ticket

fields.description: Managed exclusively by the transition() controller method — never editable via a plain save, see validate()'s content-lock.
fields.label: Status
fields.options:
Draft
Active
Returned
Rejected
Withdrawn
Completed

fields.description: The workflow step key this requisition is currently sitting at (waiting for that step's actor), or the step it stalled/finalized at for a non-Active status. See capital_purchase_requisition.py's REQUISITION_WORKFLOW for the fixed chain.
fields.label: Current Step

fields.description: Full transition history — every submit/advance/reject/return/resubmit/withdraw action, who did it, when, and the reason if one was required. Doubles as the milestone-timestamp record (each row's timestamp is that step's milestone) rather than a separate Datetime field per step.
fields.label: Transition History
